key_concepts: Alfred Wegener proposed the Continental Drift Theory in 1912.
Continents were once joined in a supercontinent called Pangaea.
The coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces.
Matching rock formations and mountain ranges across continents support continental drift.

Mesosaurus was a coastal reptile that could not have crossed the Atlantic Ocean.
Cynognathus and Lystrosaurus were land animals incapable of migrating across oceans.
Glossopteris had large bulky seeds that could not drift or fly across oceans.
Glacial marks and coal deposits in Antarctica indicate it once had a warmer climate.
Coal deposits in Antarctica suggest it was once located near the equator.
